groups.reason: publish.mjs records --out's HEAD before step 6 changes anything. When the public CI's scan fails after the commit, it resets --out to that commit (git reset --hard; --out was checked clean beforehand, so nothing of the operator's is lost). On an unborn branch it deletes the ref, empties the index and removes the shipped files. The stop message says the commit was undone, or that undoing it failed and must be done by hand, so it no longer asks for a hand reset --soft. The scan reads --out's whole history, so it still runs on the commit; I-6 allows 'before or as part of committing'. A failing result now blocks the commit. The 'committed ... not pushed' line is printed only after the scan passes. Red: the new test 'a failing public scan blocks the commit' failed with HEAD left at the rejected commit. Green: it passes.

summary: I fixed both groups on the work list, G-10 and G-11, as one cluster c1 (scripts/publish.mjs plus tests/regression-publish.test.mjs). I captured the red and green with test_one on tests/regression-publish.test.mjs. Three new tests failed before the fix, each for the reason its finding names: the rejected commit was left at HEAD, nothing was recorded in --out, and a snapshot with no scanner was committed. All three pass after it. The full suite was not run by this node; the runner runs it. After a public-scan failure, publish now undoes its own commit and leaves --out at its earlier release. It refuses a snapshot that ships no scripts/check-secrets.mjs before touching --out. It records the scan's output in --out's git directory. Two LOW items are deferred: a failed git add or commit in step 6 still leaves --out dirty, and the scan order in ROADMAP D2 is out of date, which is outside this node's globs. The groups the operator deferred (G-1, G-2, G-3, G-4, G-7) were left alone.
